repairs.evidenceText: ECE's official 2026 appliance form verifies $75 new refrigerator/freezer with recycling, $50 recycling only, $25 dehumidifier, $25 electric dryer, and $25 Wi-Fi smart thermostat rows; the same rows were visually checked in the PDF screenshot. ECE's EV page links to the 2026 EV PDF, which verifies a $400 bill credit for a metered Level 2 home charger on time-of-use or off-peak storage with an outside meter and primary-residence limitation; the PDF screenshot also matches the extracted row. ([East Central Energy][1]) ECE's 2026 ASHP application verifies $750 ducted/hybrid high-efficiency, $1,000 ducted/hybrid 2026 CEE Tier 1, $200 ductless <=1 ton, and $500 ductless >1 ton rows; ECE's ASHP info sheet separately verifies the $40/ton QI adder. ECE's 2026 GSHP application verifies $400 per ton for ENERGY STAR listed geothermal or ground source heat pumps, with contractor signature and installation verification requirements. The HPWH blocker is resolved by replacing the stale landing-page/form source with the direct official 2026 HPWH PDF: the landing page still shows a 2025 deadline and links to a 2025 form, but ECE's official 2026 HPWH PDF is accessible, text-readable, visually checked, and verifies a $500 rebate for a minimum 50 gallon ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater with field check required. ([East Central Energy][2]) ECE's general rules confirm first-come, first-served funding, current-program-year/service-area requirements, bill credit timing under $1,000, one rebate per appliance type per account, and ECE installation confirmation for ASHP, GSHP, and HPWH. ([East Central Energy][3])
repairs.reasoningNotes: The prior human-review reason in the uploaded target concerned the heat pump water heater page not exposing the same current-year form text as other ECE measures; that is resolved for calculation-package purposes by using the direct official 2026 HPWH PDF as the authoritative source instead of the stale HPWH landing-page link. Target context reviewed from the uploaded prompt.  The rate rows are prescriptive and deterministic once RetroFi has the required selectedMeasure, unitCount, tons, equipmentTier, ENERGY STAR status, ECE account/service-area eligibility, appliance recycling status, and EV TOU/off-peak enrollment inputs. Standard funding availability, receipt, model-number, contractor-signature, ENERGY STAR/AHRI verification, and ECE installation-check requirements should remain eligibility notes or missing-input gates, but they do not require custom/quote-only review and do not justify suppressing the effect by default when the measure-catalog inputs are present.

humanReviewReasons: Current Grand Marais PUC 2026 sources do not support the existing Bright Energy Solutions ChargePoint/Home Flex EV charger catalog for this opportunity.

The current Grand Marais 2026 rebate summary shows EV Chargers as a separate ENERGY STAR Level 2 Connected measure with a $15 rebate, while the $150-$500 amount range applies to a separate EV Charging Rate Enrollment incentive.

The existing effect should be recoded or split before default inclusion: one effect for the $15 connected Level 2 EV charger rebate, and a separate effect for the $500 first-household/$150 additional-EV time-of-use EV charging rate enrollment incentive.

Grand Marais Google Drive source forms were accessible visually through the Drive viewer but are image-based/dynamic rather than text-readable; keep review until the source package can preserve the corrected rows and citations.

verifiedMeasureRows.measureName: Grand Marais PUC 2026 EV Chargers - ENERGY STAR Level 2 Connected
verifiedMeasureRows.rateFormula: $15 per new qualifying connected Level 2 EV charger.
verifiedMeasureRows.eligibilityNotes: Must be a new ENERGY STAR-qualified, AC-output Level 2 EV charger with connected-capable functionality. Custom or self-built chargers do not qualify. Customer must own, lease, or have ordered a battery EV or plug-in hybrid EV, and the charger must be fully installed and operational before submitting the application. Receipt/invoice or installed-charger nameplate documentation must show make, model, serial number, purchase date, and cost. This is not the $150/$500 Bright Energy Solutions ChargePoint catalog row.

verifiedMeasureRows.measureName: Grand Marais PUC 2026 EV Charging Rate Enrollment - first qualifying household enrollment
verifiedMeasureRows.rateFormula: $500 one-time incentive for an EV owner who enrolls in the Grand Marais time-of-use EV charging rate.
verifiedMeasureRows.eligibilityNotes: Must be a residential electric customer of Grand Marais Utilities, own a qualifying EV, commit to participate in the time-of-use EV charging rate for at least 12 months if continuing to own the EV, and have a separate meter socket installed to monitor EV charger usage. Form states one $500 enrollment incentive per household.

verifiedMeasureRows.measureName: Grand Marais PUC 2026 EV Charging Rate Enrollment - additional qualifying EV
verifiedMeasureRows.rateFormula: $150 incentive for each additional qualifying EV owned by a household participating in the Grand Marais time-of-use EV charging rate.
verifiedMeasureRows.eligibilityNotes: Applies to additional qualifying EVs under the same EV charging rate enrollment program. Requires Grand Marais residential electric customer status, qualifying EV ownership, time-of-use EV charging rate participation, and separate EV charger metering.

repairs.evidenceText: Grand Marais official city page says Grand Marais Public Utility and SMMPA offer rebates and directs users to SMMPA for the full rebate list; SMMPA's Grand Marais page lists 2026 Residential Rebates including an ENERGY STAR EV Chargers Form and separately lists an EV Charging Rate Enrollment Form under Residential Other Resources. ([Grand Marais][1]) The current Grand Marais 2026 rebate summary visually shows EV Chargers as ENERGY STAR Level 2 Connected with a $15 rebate and a separate EV Charging Rate Enrollment row with $150-$500. The Grand Marais 2026 EV charger application visually states REBATE = $15 per Charger and lists connected Level 2 ENERGY STAR eligibility requirements. The Grand Marais EV Charging Rate form visually states a $500 incentive for EV owners enrolling in the TOU EV charging rate and a $150 incentive for each additional qualifying EV, with one $500 enrollment incentive per household. The generic Bright Energy Solutions page still states a different $500 Wi-Fi-enabled ChargePoint Home Flex/$150 other qualifying Level 2 charger offer, but that is not the current local Grand Marais measure row verified in the 2026 Grand Marais forms. ([Bright Energy Solutions][2])
repairs.reasoningNotes: The uploaded target package describes a Bright Energy Solutions 2026 EV charger catalog with $150-$500 amounts and existing human-review suppression.  Current Grand Marais-specific 2026 official materials show that the same $150-$500 range belongs to EV Charging Rate Enrollment, not EV charger purchase/installation, while the EV charger rebate is $15 per connected ENERGY STAR Level 2 charger. Therefore the existing effect should not be promoted into user-facing totals by default. The source blocker is not simply removable; the effect needs a source/model repair and likely a measure split.
